title: Preparatory Quiz 2: Śrīla Prabhupāda on Community & Devotee Care
description: 20 questions on Śrīla Prabhupāda's vision for community, cooperation, and devotee care.

questions.question: In his final months in Vrindavan (1977), when disciples asked Śrīla Prabhupāda how they could demonstrate their genuine love and gratitude for him after his departure, what was his defining instruction?
options: By constructing the largest marble temples across major world capitals
By distributing more books than any other religious movement in history
By showing how much they could lovingly cooperate together to maintain the society
By practicing strict solitary asceticism in the sacred forests of Vraja
questions.explanation: In Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta and TKG's Diary, Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly emphasized to his disciples: 'Your love for me will be shown by how much you cooperate with each other to keep this institution together.'
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 6, 'Vrindavana Days' (1977)

questions.question: According to Śrīla Prabhupāda's letters and teachings on community health, which qualities are essential for sustaining harmony and preventing devotee attrition in temples? (Select all that apply)
options: Affectionate leadership where leaders act like caring parents rather than bureaucratic bosses
Rigid corporate management enforcing strict financial quotas over personal well-being
Mutual appreciation of every devotee's service without imposing material hierarchy
Forbearance and forgiveness when interpersonal friction or misunderstandings arise
questions.explanation: Śrīla Prabhupāda taught that ISKCON is a spiritual family sustained by love, trust, parental care from leaders, and mutual appreciation (Letter to Gurudāsa, 1970; Letter to Satsvarūpa, 1971). Impersonal corporate management that treats devotees like mechanical tools undermines community life.
questions.reference: Letters to Gurudāsa (March 15, 1970) and Satsvarūpa (August 10, 1971)

questions.question: True or False: Śrīla Prabhupāda taught that a devotee should cultivate the mentality of a honeybee (seeking the good and virtues in others) rather than a fly (seeking open sores and faults), warning that fault-finding destroys spiritual community.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: In room conversations and letters, Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly emphasized that a Vaiṣṇava should be like a honeybee, focusing exclusively on the devotional service and virtues of Godbrothers and Godsisters, rather than like a fly, which ignores the beautiful body to sit on an infection.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5; Room Conversation, Bombay, 1974

questions.question: Who am I based on these clues?
clues: I held a degree in mechanical engineering from Ohio State University and drove a taxi in San Francisco before meeting Śrīla Prabhupāda in 1967.
I gladly stepped down from temple management because I preferred driving the saṅkīrtana van, building Ratha-yātrā carts, and taking out the trash.
Śrīla Prabhupāda praised me as an ideal saint whose humble, selfless service united devotees, saying my picture should be placed on Ratha-yātrā carts.
options: Viṣṇujana Swami
Jayānanda Ṭhākura (Jim Kohr)
Hayagrīva Dāsa
Tamāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami
questions.explanation: Jayānanda Ṭhākura renounced worldly prestige to perform humble services like building carts, driving vans, and emptying garbage. He avoided praise and united devotees through unpretentious love, earning Śrīla Prabhupāda's deepest glorification.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 6; Jayānanda Ṭhākura ACBSP

questions.question: Identify the speaker and context of this foundational instruction on spiritual leadership:
questions.quote: Now all of you GBC and temple presidents must sit down together and chalk out a plan... Our leadership is not based on corporate domination, but on love and trust.
questions.context: Letter on spiritual administration and the nature of authority in ISKCON
options: Tamāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami to the temple presidents of the Rādhā-Dāmodara Party
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura to the governing managers of the Gauḍīya Maṭha
Satsvarūpa dāsa Goswami addressing the Dallas Gurukula staff
Śrīla Prabhupāda writing to his GBC members and temple presidents
questions.explanation: In his correspondence with GBC members and temple presidents (e.g., Letter to Girirāja, August 1972), Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly clarified that spiritual authority in ISKCON must operate through love and trust rather than force, bureaucratic manipulation, or commercial dominance.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda Letter to Girirāja (August 12, 1972); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4

questions.question: Arrange these foundational milestones in the historical expansion of ISKCON's communities in chronological order (from earliest to latest):
items: Establishment of New Vrindaban as ISKCON's pioneer rural farm community in West Virginia
Official formation of the Governing Body Commission (GBC) to oversee worldwide community management
Opening of the first storefront temple at 26 Second Avenue ('Matchless Gifts') in New York City
Laying the cornerstone and founding of the world headquarters at Śrī Māyāpur Candrodaya Mandir
questions.explanation: The chronological progression of ISKCON community structures began with the first storefront temple at 26 Second Avenue (1966), followed by the first rural community at New Vrindaban (1968), the formalization of the GBC management body (1970), and the establishment of the international spiritual headquarters in Śrī Dhāma Māyāpura (1972).
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vols. 2–5

questions.question: Match each historic community or project with its primary spiritual purpose as designated by Śrīla Prabhupāda:
right: The 'Transcendental United Nations' designed to unite all nations in congregational chanting
The storefront 'Matchless Gifts' where Prabhupāda first cooked and served disciples like a father
Pioneer rural sanctuary established in 1968 for plain living, high thinking, and cow protection
Model farm project established in 1976 showcasing self-sufficiency, ox-power, and varṇāśrama
questions.explanation: New Vrindaban (1968) demonstrated early cow protection and rural simplicity; Gita Nagari (1976) was planned as a model self-sufficient farm; 26 Second Avenue was the first urban temple family; and Mayapur was envisioned as the 'Transcendental United Nations.'
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vols. 2, 3, 5, 6

questions.question: Analyze the relationship between individual individuality and collective spiritual unity:
questions.assertion: Śrīla Prabhupāda taught that unity within a spiritual society does not require the elimination of individual personality or healthy diversity.
questions.reason: Spiritual unity is achieved when diverse individuals coordinate their unique capacities by placing Kṛṣṇa and the order of the spiritual master at the center of their activities.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly rejected impersonal uniformity. In his letters and talks, he explained that variety is the mother of enjoyment; in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, devotees retain their individuality and distinct talents, but achieve sublime unity by harmonizing everything in the service of the Lord.
questions.reference: Letter to Brahmānanda (1969); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4

questions.question: Read the following statements regarding Śrīla Prabhupāda's policy on devotee care and identify the INCORRECT statement:
questions.passage:
1. Temple presidents should treat devotees as sacred trusts sent by Kṛṣṇa for training and protection.
2. If a devotee experiences spiritual difficulties, leaders must patiently encourage, counsel, and support them.
3. If a devotee fails to meet high book distribution quotas, leaders should immediately expel them to protect temple finances.
4. The spiritual master suffers grief whenever a disciple falters or leaves the community.
options: Treating devotees as sacred trusts sent by Kṛṣṇa for training and protection
Patiently encouraging, counseling, and supporting struggling devotees
Expelling devotees immediately if they miss book distribution quotas
The spiritual master experiencing personal grief whenever a disciple falters
questions.explanation: The third statement is completely false. Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly rebuked leaders who treated devotees harshly or expelled them over performance issues. He wrote that losing a devotee is a great failure on the part of leadership, emphasizing that devotees are not machines to be discarded for lack of production.
questions.reference: Letter to Jagadīśa (1972); Letter to Satsvarūpa (1971); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5

questions.question: Identify the missing link in Śrīla Prabhupāda's formula for healthy community expansion:
chain: Hearing and chanting in the temple
Cultivating personal purity and mutual respect
Inspiring the broader public to join a loving, functional spiritual family
options: Imposing strict central financial control over all individual property
Joyful, unified cooperation among devotees in executing preaching missions
Eliminating all administrative differences through forced homogenization
Confining all devotional activities strictly within temple walls
questions.explanation: Prabhupāda taught that personal purification and internal cooperation naturally manifest as effective, attractive outreach. When the public sees devotees working together in genuine love and harmony, they are drawn to take shelter of Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
questions.reference: Letter to Kīrtanānanda (1969); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4

questions.question: Which of the following traits is the ODD ONE OUT because it directly undermines Vaiṣṇava community life according to Śrīla Prabhupāda?
options: Kṣamā (Forgiveness of Godbrothers' minor shortcomings and past mistakes)
Dāsya-bhāva (Viewing oneself as the servant of all other devotees)
Śraddhā (Firm faith in the instructions of the spiritual master)
Pratiṣṭhā-āśā (The burning ambition for personal fame, title, and managerial prestige)
questions.explanation: Pratiṣṭhā-āśā (the desire for personal prestige, honor, and managerial distinction) is identified by the Ācāryas as 'subtle sex' and the root cause of factionalism, envy, and disintegration in devotee communities. The other three qualities foster harmony and community cohesion.
questions.reference: Sri Bhaktisiddhanta Vaibhava; Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5

questions.question: According to Śrīla Prabhupāda's letter to his disciple Gurudāsa (March 15, 1970), what is the direct spiritual consequence when devotees abandon fault-finding and appreciate one another's diverse services?
options: Kṛṣṇa accepts their collective offering and empowers their unified preaching, removing material barriers between their services
The community becomes an elite intellectual council that no longer requires temple worship
Devotees automatically achieve mystic perfection (siddhis) without needing to study scripture
Management duties become redundant and can be completely eliminated
questions.explanation: In his famous letter to Gurudāsa, Prabhupāda wrote that Kṛṣṇa sees sincerity, not material size or status. When devotees recognize that a calf's service and Rādhārāṇī's service are both accepted by the Lord, and avoid criticizing each other, Kṛṣṇa is deeply pleased and empowers their preaching.
questions.reference: Letter to Gurudāsa (March 15, 1970); Servant of the Servant

questions.question: Examine these three statements regarding Śrīla Prabhupāda's vision for ISKCON's GBC and leadership. Select the statement that is FALSE:
options: Prabhupāda formed the GBC in 1970 to relieve himself of day-to-day administrative burdens so he could focus on translating his books.
Prabhupāda directed that temple presidents should govern their communities primarily by exercising autocratic command and threat of excommunication.
Prabhupāda envisioned the GBC meeting annually in Mayapur to resolve global challenges through consensus, prayer, and cooperative planning.
questions.explanation: The second statement is completely false. Prabhupāda explicitly warned leaders against acting as autocrats, dictators, or bosses. He instructed that a Vaiṣṇava leader must lead by personal example, humility, love, and affectionate guidance.
questions.reference: GBC Resolution (July 28, 1970); Letter to Upendra (1971); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4

questions.question: How did Śrīla Prabhupāda resolve this historic community dispute?
questions.scenario: In the early 1970s, severe managerial friction developed between certain temple presidents and book distribution leaders over the allocation of funds, temple manpower, and living conditions. When the matter was brought before Śrīla Prabhupāda, both groups felt their service was superior.
options: He dissolved the traveling parties and ordered all devotees to remain strictly confined within city temples under local management
He permanently banned the temple presidents from holding administrative posts and appointed external corporate auditors

He brought the parties together, reminded them that both book distribution and temple deity worship are essential limbs of Lord Caitanya's mission, and insisted they cooperate by balancing temple maintenance with field saṅkīrtana
He declared that temple management was completely irrelevant and directed everyone to become independent itinerant mendicants
questions.explanation: In Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta and Servant of the Servant, when tensions arose between temple leaders and traveling saṅkīrtana parties (like the Rādhā-Dāmodara party), Prabhupāda did not take a sectarian side. He affirmed that both temple worship (pāñcarātriki-vidhi) and public preaching (bhāgavata-vidhi) are like two parallel train tracks, demanding mutual respect, cooperation, and balanced resource-sharing.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 6; Servant of the Servant, Ch. 15

questions.question: Based on Śrīla Prabhupāda's instructions on community etiquette, what is the proper course of action in this situation?
questions.scenario: Two department heads in a temple community hold strongly opposing viewpoints on how to design a festival budget, and their disagreement is beginning to create anxiety and polarization among younger devotees.
options: Lobby temple members behind closed doors to build a political faction and force a public vote against the opposing leader
Discuss the matter respectfully in a spirit of service, refer to guru-sādhu-śāstra with senior authorities, and amicably compromise for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa and the peace of the temple
Immediately resign from all devotional service and move away to start a rival, independent center
Launch a public campaign during temple classes to expose the personal defects of the other department head
questions.explanation: Śrīla Prabhupāda taught that devotees must always discuss disagreements respectfully without factionalism or personal malice. If an impasse occurs, they should seek guidance from senior Vaiṣṇavas and compromise, knowing that maintaining temple harmony and pleasing the spiritual master far outweighs winning a managerial debate.
questions.reference: Letter to Hamsadūta (1969); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4

questions.question: In a letter to his disciple Satsvarūpa (August 10, 1971), Śrīla Prabhupāda wrote: 'Our men should not be treated like karmīs... If we lose one devotee, it is a great, great loss. Therefore we must take care of them very nicely.' What fundamental principle of devotee care does this primary document establish?
options: Temples should lower their spiritual standards so that nobody ever feels challenged or uncomfortable
Devotees who join are temporary workers whose utility expires once they show physical exhaustion
Secular economic efficiency is more important than personal spiritual relationships
Devotees are precious spiritual souls who must be nurtured with personal affection, guidance, and spiritual shelter, not exploited for labor
questions.explanation: Prabhupāda's letter establishes that a devotee is not an employee or a disposable worker ('karmī'). A spiritual community must cherish every individual soul who surrenders their life to Kṛṣṇa, providing compassionate care, spiritual guidance, and a loving shelter.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda Letter to Satsvarūpa (August 10, 1971); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5

questions.question: Who am I based on these clues?
clues: In 1968, my Godbrother and I traveled into the rugged, roadless hills of Marshall County, West Virginia, living in a primitive farmhouse without running water or electricity.
Along with Hayagrīva Dāsa, I helped establish ISKCON's first rural community, clearing brush, caring for our first cow (Kālyāṇī), and preparing the ground for Prabhupāda's arrival in 1969.
Prabhupāda wrote to me repeatedly, giving detailed visions of 'simple living and high thinking' as an alternative to modern urban chaos.
options: Kīrtanānanda Swami
Jayapatākā Swami
Śyāmasundara Dāsa
Mukunda Goswami
questions.explanation: In 1968, Kīrtanānanda Swami and Hayagrīva Dāsa pioneered New Vrindaban in West Virginia, clearing wilderness and tending to the first cow, Kālyāṇī. Prabhupāda visited the community in 1969, spending a month living simply and outlining his vision for rural self-sufficiency.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 4, Ch. 33 ('New Vrindaban')

questions.question: Identify the speaker of this urgent appeal for devotional unity:
questions.quote: If we fight among ourselves, how will we preach to the world? Our unity is our strength.
questions.context: Urgent appeal given during leadership meetings in Calcutta and Bombay amidst rapid worldwide expansion
options: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in Jaiva-dharma
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura to the governing trustees in 1936
Śrīla Prabhupāda addressing his disciples during crucial leadership meetings in India
Tamāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami addressing the temple presidents of North America
questions.explanation: During crucial periods of expansion in the early 1970s when leadership disputes threatened projects in India (Mayapur and Bombay), Śrīla Prabhupāda repeatedly warned his disciples that internal strife would ruin their ability to convince the world. 'Our unity is our strength' was his urgent call to all leaders.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5; Conversations in Calcutta (1971)

questions.question: Which of the following were direct, practical instructions given by Śrīla Prabhupāda to ensure the health, stability, and protection of devotees living in temple communities? (Select all that apply)
options: Requiring all householders to immediately renounce family life and take sannyāsa regardless of age
Providing wholesome, freshly prepared prasādam, adequate rest, and clean living quarters for all residents
Forbidding children from learning reading or writing to keep their minds free of material thoughts
Establishing proper education and loving protection for children (Gurukula) as the society's most sacred duty
questions.explanation: Prabhupāda insisted that devotees must be nourished with nutritious prasādam and clean, peaceful living conditions. He also designated child protection and education (Gurukula) as one of ISKCON's highest, most sacred responsibilities. He did not mandate forced sannyāsa for householders, nor did he ban basic literacy.
questions.reference: Letters on Health and Diet (1970–1976); Letter to Bhānu (1972); Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 5

questions.question: In his ultimate vision for ISKCON as an enduring spiritual society, how did Śrīla Prabhupāda define the true purpose of its temples, farm communities, and administrative bodies?
options: To build a powerful political voting bloc capable of influencing international secular governments
To provide a loving, educational shelter where sincere souls can be trained in pure bhakti and return together back to Godhead
To create an exclusive, isolated commune that cuts off all communication with modern society
To amass commercial assets and wealth to compete with global financial conglomerates
questions.explanation: In Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta and his official declarations, Śrīla Prabhupāda defined ISKCON not as a worldly enterprise, but as an educational, spiritual sanctuary where conditioned souls can find shelter, awaken their dormant love for Kṛṣṇa, and practice cooperative devotional service to return back to Godhead.
questions.reference: Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, Vol. 6, Ch. 52 ('The Last Days')
